title: Farmer's Breakfast Casserole
subtitle: Hash browns, sausage, eggs, and cheese baked in one deep dish.
description: Sausage, hash browns, and cheese under a blanket of eggs in a deep pan. The farmhouse breakfast casserole every crew recognizes.

ingredients.name: sliced green onions
ingredients.notes: plus hot sauce at the line

steps.title: Gather ingredients and equipment
steps.instruction: Line up every ingredient for Farmer's Breakfast Casserole in the order you will cook — measure spices into ramekins, trim proteins on a dedicated board, and set tongs, thermometers, and hotel pans within arm's reach before any heat goes on. Double-check seasoning after scaling — crew palates run salty after long shifts, so taste the first portion before opening the line.

steps.title: Preheat ovens and surfaces
steps.instruction: Preheat ovens, griddles, or grills to recipe temp before the crew arrives — cold equipment extends cook time and dries out batch Sausage. Confirm burners ignite evenly and sheet pans are greased or lined.

steps.title: Heat the oven
steps.instruction: Heat oven to 375°F. Grease a deep 9x13 pan or hotel half-pan. Thaw hash browns completely and squeeze out excess water in a clean towel—wet potatoes make a soggy casserole.

steps.title: Brown the sausage
steps.instruction: Cook breakfast sausage in a skillet over medium-high, breaking into small crumbles until no pink remains and internal temperature reaches 160°F. Drain on paper towels.

steps.title: Layer the base
steps.instruction: Spread hash browns evenly in the pan. Top with sausage and half the cheddar. Whisk eggs, milk, mustard, salt, and pepper until uniform and pour evenly over the layers.

steps.title: Bake until set
steps.instruction: Cover with foil and bake 25 minutes. Uncover, top with remaining cheddar, and bake 15 more until center reaches 165°F on a thermometer and top is golden.

steps.title: Verify safe internal temps
steps.instruction: Spot-check the thickest pieces with an instant-read thermometer — target 165°F. If any piece reads low, return it to heat immediately rather than holding under temp on the line.

steps.title: Hold for call interruptions
steps.instruction: If tones drop mid-service, cover finished food and hold at 140°F in a warm cabinet or 200°F oven — never leave proteins below 140°F for more than 30 minutes cumulative. Note the hold time on the pan with a grease pencil.

steps.title: Portion and open the line
steps.instruction: Portion Farmer's Breakfast Casserole onto sheet trays or hotel pans for family-style service. Stack plates, forks, and napkins at the end of the line so late-arriving crew can self-serve without bottlenecking the cook.

steps.title: Scale for larger halls
steps.instruction: When cooking for more than 8 firefighters, split into two pans halfway through so the bottom layer does not overcook while the top waits — duplicate mise en place if you double batches.

steps.title: Rest and portion
steps.instruction: Rest casserole 10 minutes before cutting so slices hold clean squares. Garnish with green onions and serve with hot sauce at the line.

steps.title: Final quality check before service
steps.instruction: Walk the line once before opening service for Farmer's Breakfast Casserole — confirm hotel pans are labeled, backup trays are in the 200°F oven, and thermometers are calibrated. Rookies should ask a senior cook to spot-check the first portion.

stationWorkflow: Squeeze hash browns dry—this is the single biggest factor in a crisp versus soggy base.
Cover for the first half of baking so top cheese does not over-brown before center sets.
Cut with a sharp bench scraper in the pan for even ten-portion squares.
cleanupNotes: Soak the 9x13 with hot water while still warm before baked egg residue sets.
Drain sausage grease into a heat-safe container, never down the sink.
leftovers: Reheat portions covered at 325°F for 12 minutes until steaming in the center.
Cube leftovers into breakfast burrito filling with salsa and extra cheese.
